learning_outcomes.text: Have knowledge and understanding of the principles of multivariable calculus and the basic theory of linear differential equations that underpin mechanical engineering.
Be able to apply their knowledge and understanding to identify, formulate and solve mathematical problems of multivariable calculus and basic linear differential equations using established methods.
Be able to choose and apply relevant analytical and modeling methods in both multivariable calculus and basic linear differential equations.
Be able to select and use appropriate tools and methods to solve mathematical problems formulated in terms of multivariable calculus or basic linear differential equations.
Be able to combine theory and practice to solve mathematical problems of multivariable calculus and basic linear differential equations theory.
Understand applicable methods and techniques in multivariable calculus and basic linear differential equations and their limitations.
Knowledge and understanding of the scientific and mathematical principles that underpin their branch of engineering.
The ability to apply their knowledge and understanding to identify, formulate and solve engineering problems using established methods.
The ability to select and use appropriate equipment, tools and methods.
The ability to combine theory and practice to solve engineering problems.

That students have demonstrated possession and understanding of knowledge in a field of study that builds on general secondary education, and is usually found at a level that, although supported by advanced textbooks, also includes some aspects that imply knowledge from the forefront of their field of study.

That students know how to apply their knowledge to their work or vocation in a professional way and possess the competences that are usually demonstrated by elaborating and defending arguments and solving problems within their field of study.
Ability to solve problems with initiative, decision-making, creativity, critical reasoning and to communicate and transmit knowledge, skills and abilities in the field of Industrial Engineering.

Ability to solve mathematical problems that may arise in engineering. Aptitude to apply knowledge about: linear algebra; geometry; differential geometry; differential and integral calculus; differential and partial differential equations; numerical methods; numerical algorithms; statistics and optimization.

assessment_rules: The evaluation will be based on two partial controls (40%) and a final exam (60%). No AI tools are allowed in this course.
